comments.comment: Great video. I'm in the middle of making it now. Some first timer experience: A) Even if you intend to make only one loaf and wanna half the quantities - do not! Half the dough is going to be wasted because it sticks to anything that it touches, so the final  dough that stays in one peace is quite small. B) Prepare two poolishes - it takes long and if you decide to retry after all the dough got wasted/washed off your hands, you want another poolish ready right away. C) the stage where the dough is being picked up at 03:33 is harder than it looks, you try to pick it and it just pulls and tears and a lot gets stuck to the hand. More flour and some more folds allowed forming a pickable piece. And the time that it takes to pull-fold and then pick-rotate-flip-drop - 30 minutes while in the video it looks like a single minute. D) Since i was so slow on the previous stage, should i still let the dough rest the same time before the second folding? E)  Wetting the hands too many times or doing it after there is already much dough stuck to your hands - causes the dough to become moist and more sticky. F) The stage where you pull the sides and tuck below - do not pull too tight or it will tear on top or on the side. And then - remixing, refolding an retucking. Another half an hour. And a dough of kinda wrong consistensy because of all the flour that it picked from the work surface. G) Liberately flouring - do not be too liberal or it will cause the crust be covered under flour and you won't know what color it even is. H) A towel instead of gloves is not enough with the dutch oven. There IS moisture inside it - it's invisible. 250 degrees C is A LOT hotter than the usual 150-170 that most dishes cook at, so there is not even a trace of vapor condensate - just surprisingly hot steamy air. I) When you scar the loaf - pay at least some attention to the shape, so that you do not get an unintentional swastika or zeta symbol. K) Overall - nice, thick crunchy crust. My wife really liked the bread.
